title: Marvel Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Marvel wells have a 110 ft median depth, with drilling and a finished system estimated from $5,500 to $20,200.
h1: What Marvel, Colorado Wells Are Like
intro_html:
If you are buying land or a home near Marvel, the nearby permit record gives a useful starting point: wells have a 110-foot median depth, and reported yields have a 10.0 gallons-per-minute median. Most permits are for domestic or household use, and most wells are completed in unnamed fractured-bedrock aquifers.

These records cover permitted wells within five miles of Marvel in La Plata County. They are not a guarantee for a particular lot. Local geology can change quickly, so use the data to frame a driller’s bid, then verify the parcel, access, septic layout, water rights and neighboring well performance.

sections.heading: Marvel well depth depends on the local ground
sections.html:
Reported well depths around Marvel center on 110 feet. The middle half runs from 60 to 161 feet, while the deepest reported well reaches 830 feet. Depth is not uniform across the area: 42% of reported wells are under 100 feet, 48% fall from 100 to 300 feet, and 10% are from 300 to 600 feet.

That spread matters when you compare drilling bids. A bid based on the median may fit many sites, but a lot that misses productive fractures can require substantially more drilling. The records identify mostly unnamed fractured-bedrock aquifer wells, with only a few alluvial and Mancos entries. Fractured rock can produce water unevenly, even between nearby properties.

sections.heading: Expected well yield near Marvel
sections.html:
Only 82 wells in the permit records report a pump yield, so the yield statistics are useful but limited. Among those reports, the median is 10.0 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 4.7 to 14.0 gallons per minute. Half of reported wells produce between those figures during the recorded test or measurement.

One percent of reported wells are under 1 gallon per minute. Another 24% fall from 1 to 5 gallons per minute, 50% from 5 to 15, and 24% produce more than 15. A buyer should ask for the neighbor’s well log and pumping information, not rely only on the area median. Storage tanks can help with a modest-producing well, but they do not fix a dry or unreliable source.

sections.heading: Water levels recorded around Marvel
sections.html:
Only 18 wells report a static water level, so this part of the record is thinner than the depth data. The median depth to static water is 50 feet, and the middle half runs from 40 to 59 feet. That describes the water level in the reporting wells at the time measured; it is not the same as well depth and should not be treated as a parcel-wide groundwater elevation.

The available facts do not provide a water-level series by decade, so they do not establish that the water table is dropping near Marvel. Ask for the original well construction report, static level, pumping rate and recovery information for nearby wells. A driller can also evaluate whether the proposed well location is likely to encounter the same fractures or water-bearing material.

sections.heading: Marvel’s permit history and local drillers
sections.html:
Permit activity is spread across several decades. Records show one permit in the 1960s, 73 in the 1970s, 101 in the 1980s, 169 in the 1990s, 171 in the 2000s, 61 in the 2010s, and 23 in the 2020s. The newest permit year in the data is 2025.

The most active names in these records are Beeman Bros Drilling Inc, including J. L. Beeman with 62 records and Matthew N. Beeman with 45, plus Holgate Drilling Co., including Merle Holgate with 58. Those counts show local permit history, not a recommendation or proof of current availability. Confirm licensing, insurance, references and who will handle the pump, testing and paperwork.

sections.heading: What a new well may cost near Marvel
sections.html:
The local cost model assumes mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground. Typical drilling is estimated at $50 to $75 per foot. At the area’s 110-foot median depth, the drilled hole works out to about $5,500 to $8,200. That is only the drilling portion.

A finished system, including the pump, pressure tank, trenching and electrical, is estimated at about $11,500 to $20,200 at the median depth. A deeper hole, difficult access, extra casing or more complicated trenching can move the actual bid higher. Get a written proposal that separates footage, casing, grout, pump equipment, testing, electrical and site restoration. Ask what happens if the hole is dry or the yield is below the target.

sections.heading: Risks to check before buying or building
sections.html:
Low yield is not the only concern. The mapped area within about ten miles includes five PFAS sampling or contamination sites and five historic mine features. There are zero EPA Superfund or cleanup sites mapped in the supplied data, but that does not make every private well automatically safe. Test the water for common household concerns and for contaminants appropriate to the parcel’s location and history.

Most permits are domestic or household use at 89%, with stock use at 11% and irrigation at 1%. Confirm the permit’s allowed use before planning landscaping, livestock or additional dwellings. Have the well location, septic system and building footprint reviewed together. Setbacks, access for drilling equipment, casing and grout condition, and the possibility of a dry hole should all be addressed before closing or excavation.

sections.heading: A practical plan for a Marvel lot
sections.html:
Start with the Colorado DWR permit record for the parcel and compare it with nearby wells toward Hesperus, Durango and other surrounding areas. The broader record contains 734 permitted wells, but only 476 are recorded as constructed, 486 report a total depth, and 82 report a pump yield. That difference is a reminder to separate documented results from assumptions.

Before buying, request neighboring well logs, water-quality results, pump information and any well-use restrictions. Have a licensed driller assess access and likely depth, and have a septic professional confirm that the proposed well, septic field and house can fit with required setbacks. If the property is in an over-appropriated basin, ask the water attorney or DWR about augmentation requirements. A good inspection reduces uncertainty; it cannot guarantee a particular fracture will produce water.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Marvel, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported well depth within five miles of Marvel is 110 feet. The middle half runs from 60 to 161 feet. Forty-two percent of reported wells are under 100 feet, while the deepest record reaches 830 feet. Most wells are in unnamed fractured-bedrock aquifers, so a neighboring depth is a guide, not a guarantee.

faq.q: How much water does a well produce in Marvel?
faq.a: Among the 82 wells that report a pump yield, the median is 10.0 gallons per minute and the middle half ranges from 4.7 to 14.0. One percent report under 1 gallon per minute. Because yield reporting is limited and fractured rock can vary, review nearby well tests and plan storage and household demand with a local driller.

faq.q: What does it cost to drill a well in Marvel?
faq.a: The local model estimates drilling at $50 to $75 per foot. At the 110-foot median depth, the drilled hole is about $5,500 to $8,200. A finished system with pump, tank, trenching and electrical is estimated at $11,500 to $20,200. Access, extra depth, casing and site conditions can change the final proposal.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Marvel?
faq.a: The permit data does not establish that a particular well is safe to drink. Five PFAS sampling or contamination sites and five historic mine features are mapped within about ten miles, with zero EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. Test a private well before use, especially near a site with a relevant land-use or mining history.
